subject: Do I have a good model if I have to run millions of iterations?

messages.author: 644133a8c0a35773
messages.subject: Do I have a good model if I have to run millions of iterations?
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am pretty new with the use of JAGS and hierarchical models. I have collected some data trough camera traps and want to perform an occupancy model. I am trying to run some models in which I use 5 covariates for the occupancy submodel and 2 for the detection submodel, nevertheless, I have had to run more than 20 millions interations to get reasonables Rhat and n.eff values. Could anyone tell me if I am doing it right?

My data consists on 63 sites (camera traps) with 14 survey ocassions (each survey ocassion = 5 days of the camera trap working fine). Although I have many NAs because the number of cameras was limited and I had to use and relocate cameras in new sites after a period of 30 days.

I would appreciate any comment or advise.

Thank you in advance.

messages.author: 6d5a0cbd55c34b88
messages.subject: Re: Do I have a good model if I have to run millions of iterations?
parts:
Hi Sandro,

Five covariates on occupancy might be a few too many for a study with 63 sites. Have you tried fitting a simpler model with a smaller number of covariates? That might be a good place to start.
If the model is still not behaving, other things to try would include centering your covariates, and trying a simpler detection model.  

Cheers,

Michael

parts:
what's the result of fitting some kind of null model.. ie, no covariates?.
20 million iterations is a pain unless reasonable.

You better try to fit simpler models and them grow them, even if this looks time consuming, but with no knowledge of the specific model, it is the best advice...

messages.author: 29d930b99cef48f0
messages.subject: Re: Do I have a good model if I have to run millions of iterations?
parts:
20 million iterations for such a small dataset suggests something is not quite right - either with the model or the data. My first guess in the troubleshooting process would be to examine the way you are defining the survey occasions. 

I think Fernando is right that you should be able to fit a null model fairly easily, i.e. constant psi and p. If you can't, there's a good chance the issue is with the data.

messages.author: 068cbc8bd5fb0d5d
messages.subject: Re: Do I have a good model if I have to run millions of iterations?
parts:
I definitely recommend simulating a test dataset and running it through the model. It's the best way to assess and troubleshoot your model. You can start with a very simple dataset and then start adding wrinkles (covariates, random noise, alternative ecological or observational processes) to test the edges of the model and see where it works and where it fails. This is a great practice to get into and in this case will help you assess whether there are data issues, model issues, or data-model mismatch issues.

Best of luck,
Daniel Hocking
